content.intro: Learn dynamic and dependent forms through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Dynamic and Dependent Forms matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines dynamic and dependent forms as part of forms and user input. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Fields that depend on other selections; Server-side option filtering; Dependent dropdowns; Progressive enhancement; Revalidating submitted relationships. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Fields that depend on other selections
items.text: Fields that depend on other selections affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Server-side option filtering
items.text: Server-side option filtering should be planned for the actual hosting topology: configuration, permissions, resource limits, observability, rollback/recovery and a testable operating procedure all matter.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
